set.body:
SCHEDULED, NOT DELIVERED. This bead exists because the review was scheduled as an in-process agent that died with its session; a schedule that does not survive the outage it is waiting on is not a schedule.

WHY IT DID NOT RUN, verbatim from the session transcript (28 occurrences):
  "idleReason":"failed"
  "failureReason":"You're out of usage credits. Run /usage-credits to keep using Fable 5.1 or /model to switch models."
Also seen: "You've hit your session limit - resets 11:50am (America/Toronto)".
This is account-level. No retry clears it; three dispatch rounds proved that and burned credits doing so.

WHAT FABLE DID DELIVER on this branch before credits ran out (so the record is accurate):
- fable-vet: plan vet, 4 blockers; it is what flagged P2b-ii as the riskiest slice
- fable-p1b: Coded/coordinate slice (320fff60) -- no blocker, 3 major
- fable-p2b: P2b-i/P2b-s -- 2 major, 6 minor

WHAT IS STILL OWED -- three slices, batch into ONE agent, model fable:
- A. P2b-ii: corpus/profile.scala + corpus-intake/CorpusReader.scala; tests CorpusReaderSuite.scala
- B. P3: corpus/link.scala; tests SegmentLinkSuite.scala
- C. P5: corpus-intake/TimebaseRepair.scala + SherlockAnnotations.scala; tests TimebaseRepairSuite.scala

POINT IT AT THESE FOUR THINGS SPECIFICALLY, not a general pass:
1. Attack the FIX, not the original bug. CorpusProfile.identity collided once (a flat count-free part vector let a variable-arity encoding straddle a sheet boundary; one sheet reading three columns and two sheets reading DIFFERENT ARTIFACTS both digested to 3880428e). Fixed by nesting. Find a fifth collision shape if one exists.
2. Verify or refute a judgement the author made about his own code: a mutant that removes the nesting but keeps the "column"/"sheet" tags SURVIVES, judged benign because arity is recoverable from the tag literal. Nobody who did not make that judgement has checked it.
3. Challenge the Memento decision: a non-monotone Coarsening is deliberately ADMITTED because Memento is cut in reverse. A reviewer wanted it refused. Engage the justification, do not merely restate the objection.
4. P5: confirm every constant that matters is READ from timebase-repair.json and that changing a value there turns a test red. partId, axisId, annotationEndSeconds and playbackStartTicks were once untested, and a test named for that file once never opened it.

METHOD (learned the hard way; see docs/design/unforgeable-types.md and AGENTS.md SD1-SD8):
- Probes must be proved from OUTSIDE the defining package. private[corpus] admits the whole storymodel4s.corpus.* tree INCLUDING corpus.intake, so a probe inside it cannot tell a closed door from an open one. Out-of-package probes live in corpus/src/test/scala/storymodel4s/consumer/.
- typeCheckErrors is a compile-time macro; Zinc records no dependency, so accessibility mutants survive unless the test scope is CLEANED first (corpusJVM/clean). Assert the file actually changed before believing a mutant.
- Every negative probe needs a positive control in the same scope. One such control failed here and taught us CorpusProfile.of is private[corpus] -- the door is shut a layer earlier than assumed.

WHAT STANDS MEANWHILE: a cold DEFAULT-MODEL review covered all three slices and found the P2b-ii blocker plus three majors, all fixed and pinned at 287f87d3 / b4ad7d20. That is not the Fable review that was asked for, and this bead is the record that it is not.

UNBLOCK: owner runs /usage-credits, or /model to switch reviewer models. Then dispatch ONE batched agent -- not one per slice. Thirteen agents were dispatched during the outage, eight redundant, and the retries themselves consumed the credits.
set.title: intake: the three risky slices still owe a FABLE review (blocked on usage credits)
